newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks shoot back up to record high.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks shoot back up to record high.

text.p: Madrid stocks closed at a record high on Friday, supported by the late Wall Street recovery on Thursday and a firm opening on Friday, dealers said.
The Spanish bourse regained all the ground lost when Wall Street shares plummetted earlier in the week.
The general index rose 10.85 points, 2.50 percent, to 445.39, a new historic record, and the Ibex-35 gained 122.59 points, 2.44 percent, to 5,141.14.
"Wall Street took us down and today, pushed by the U.S. debt recovery, allowed up to return to the starting line and a little more," one dealer said.
There was buying across all sectors after Thursday's selling session, which some dealers said was exaggerated.
The Madrid share movements resembled that of other European markets but with bigger swings, both up and down, and dealers expected some profit taking in the short term.
